questions.q: What is a Real-Time Dashboard built directly on top of?
options: KQL queries against a KQL Database — no Power BI, semantic model, or Direct Lake mode involved
A Power BI semantic model
A Fabric pipeline's Copy activity output
A Dataflow Gen2 refresh schedule
questions.explain: Each tile is one KQL query, rendered as a chart, table, or single stat.

questions.q: What makes a KQL query become a live dashboard tile?
options: Writing it in a KQL Queryset and pinning it to a dashboard
Adding it to a Fabric pipeline
Converting it to DAX first
Saving it as a Dataflow Gen2
questions.explain: That's how a query definition becomes a tile that renders and refreshes.

questions.q: What lets multiple tiles on a Real-Time Dashboard share filter logic, like a time range?
options: A base query
A semantic model relationship
A Fabric Capacity setting
The Monitoring Hub
questions.explain: Define a time range or filter once in a base query, and tiles built on top of it inherit it.

questions.q: How does cross-filtering work on a Real-Time Dashboard?
options: Clicking a bar in one tile can filter every other tile on the same dashboard, since they all query the same Eventhouse
It requires exporting to Power BI first
It only works with a semantic model's relationships
Real-Time Dashboards don't support cross-filtering at all
questions.explain: This is KQL-native cross-filtering, conceptually similar to a Power BI slicer but happening directly across tiles.

questions.q: Why does a Real-Time Dashboard tile refresh on a simple timer, while a Power BI Direct Lake report (Lesson 12) needs a separate refresh trigger concept?
options: A tile just re-issues its KQL query directly against continuously arriving data, while Direct Lake sits behind a semantic model that needs its own framing/refresh trigger
Real-Time Dashboards don't actually refresh automatically
Direct Lake mode is always faster than KQL tiles
There's no real difference between the two refresh mechanisms
questions.explain: The tile has no semantic model layer in between — it queries the Eventhouse directly on a timer.
